methodology.position_sizing: R-multiple risk-normalized, identical to tools/build_public_metrics.py -- no per-symbol dollar sizing applied.
methodology.transaction_costs: None modeled -- frictionless proxy, identical to tools/build_public_metrics.py.
methodology.no_lookahead: Entries anchored at valid_for (T+1), Mean Reversion entry = Open on valid_for, stop-first exit over the tested horizon -- identical to the corrected methodology in commit 13cb31a, generalized from a hardcoded 5 days to a horizon parameter.
methodology.multiple_comparisons_correction: Bonferroni correction, family_size=28 (7 strategies x 4 horizons = 28 tests attempted -- grown from an earlier pass's 12 (3 archetypes x 4 horizons) now that 4 more strategies are in the sweep; chosen as the family size even for cells that produce no real p-value, e.g. MOMENTUM at every horizon -- the conservative choice). p_corrected = min(1, p_raw * 28). Bonferroni (family-wise error control) was chosen over Benjamini-Hochberg (false-discovery-rate control) because this investigation's prior expectation is 'probably nothing here' and a false 'found edge' claim is the costlier mistake -- the more conservative control is the appropriate default.
methodology.seven_strategy_expansion: 3 new real archetypes (PEAD, HIGH52W_MOMENTUM, GAP_FADE_CONTINUATION) wired into scan.py/strategies/ this session -- their pre-registered rules are in strategies/pead.py, strategies/high52w_momentum.py, strategies/gap_strategy.py, committed before any backtest was run against them. They have ZERO historical signals before this session (scan.py never generated them before), so an 'insufficient data' verdict on this run is expected, not a bug -- real history starts accumulating from whichever scheduled scan first runs the updated scan.py. BASELINE_RANDOM is a 7th, backtest-only strategy: a formalized version of the random-entry-under-regime-gate control already built for the noise band (build_baseline_trades()), NOT wired into scan.py's live daily signal generation -- publishing random-stock recommendations to the live signals feed would be actively misleading; this exists purely as a directly-comparable results-table row.

verdict.verdict: no edge ever distinguishable from noise
verdict.reason: 4/17 scored windows (24%) fell outside the random-entry noise band, and the CUSUM change-point test (p=0.0950) did not find a significant break. Apparent ups and downs in the rolling metric are consistent with what a random-entry baseline under the same risk/regime rules would also produce.

Only 5 computable trades in the entire history -- too few for a meaningful rolling-window/change-point analysis (minimum 10 needed for even a single candidate break test). This is itself informative: Momentum Breakout has essentially never had enough regime-gated opportunity to generate a testable track record.

overall_verdict.TREND_PULLBACK: No edge distinguishable from noise survives Bonferroni correction at any tested horizon, though the raw (uncorrected) p-value was marginal at 10d (raw p=0.0290) -- exactly the kind of result that would look like a finding without correcting for the 28-test family this sweep runs across.
overall_verdict.MOMENTUM: Insufficient data at every tested horizon (1d=5, 3d=5, 5d=5, 10d=5 trades). Trade count doesn't change with holding-period horizon -- the same signals are just evaluated over a different forward window -- so Momentum Breakout's already-thin sample was expected to stay insufficient at every horizon, and it does.
overall_verdict.MEAN_REVERSION: No edge distinguishable from noise at any tested horizon (1d/3d/5d/10d), before or after multiple-comparisons correction. The 'no edge ever distinguishable from noise' verdict from the primary 5-day analysis is robust to holding-period choice, not an artifact of picking 5 days specifically.
